explanation: Uses Mathlib's `RiemannHypothesis`: every zero of riemannZeta (Mathlib's meromorphic continuation) other than s = 1 and the trivial zeros −2(n+1) has real part 1/2. This is the standard formulation and the Clay statement. Excluding s = 1 handles Mathlib's junk value there (it is in fact nonzero). The statement is faithful.
